label: The BASELINE MATRIX for the frozen-test rq30 grid at 16 devices: the bar the D179 shares result is read against, with the StudyPORT-EXCL port-rule exclusions applied and LISTED.
read_only: no cell run, no arm changed, no GPU, no model server; every number read through `git show` out of the committed cell, never out of a working tree
seed_0_note: Seed 0 has NO cell in this grid on this rev: every committed seed-0 cell is in the earlier `_3t`, `_rerun` or `REFUSED_preflight` families, which are a different workload and are not in this table. Seeds 1 to 3 and HOLDOUT are never read.

held_out.reason: These are the ARM UNDER TEST for StudyD179-SHARES. This table is the BAR they are read against, so they are held OUT of the baselines rather than listed among them: an arm in its own control is not a control. This is NOT a port-rule exclusion and NOT a verdict on the arm. Its cells are named here with the bar for their seed; reading them against that bar belongs to StudyD179-SHARES, not to this assembly.

cells.numbers_deliberately_not_reported_here: the headline, on-time and dashcam fields of this cell are NOT copied into this file. They are the RESULT; this file is the bar. Reading one against the other is StudyD179-SHARES's to do, and doing it here would hand that study its own comparator pre-read.

held_out.comparability_warning: a held-out cell is comparable ONLY with the baseline cells of its OWN seed, and only if its input, stack and decoding keys match theirs. Those keys are carried per row in `matrix`; the held-out cell's own code rev is given above so the check can be made rather than assumed.

inertness_read.why: the two columns a reader needs in order to tell a WORKING arm from an INERT one, summarised here so they are met before the table and not after it
inertness_read.note_on_zero_cloud_standing: These cells score the DEVICE FLOOR whatever their mechanism did: no cloud answer stands, so the headline cannot differ from the arm-independent floor. That is not by itself a port-rule failure (an arm may have escalated and had every answer arrive late, which is `confidence-cascade`'s case and is a RERUN item under D154 (5)), but it IS the signature that a number carries no information about the arm.

unscored_grid_dirs.treatment: REPORTED, not silently dropped. These directories are NOT cells: they carry no `cell.json`, so they have no headline, no on-time count and no floor, and nothing can be read from them. They are not marked INVALID either; they are unscored.
unscored_grid_dirs.consequence: the grid is UNEVEN, so an arm's absence at a seed is a GAP and not a result, and the per-seed arm count differs. Per-arm seed coverage is reported beside the matrix for exactly this reason.

seed_coverage_note: COVERAGE IS UNEVEN and is reported with its denominator rather than pooled over. An arm's absence at a seed is a GAP, not a result: it is either a seed that was never run for that arm or a directory that holds no scored cell (see `unscored_grid_dirs`). No column in this table is pooled across seeds, so no gap is averaged into a number here, but a reader who pools must pool over COMMON SUPPORT.

fields_used.hits/n: counted from cell.json -> score.score.robot_rows[].standing_correct_by_deadline, and checked to reproduce the headline rate
fields_used.single-shot (assistance) on-time: cell.json -> score.score.sweep[0].ss_pool_on_time / .ss_pool_n, at the 2.0 s single-shot deadline
fields_used.sha: the commit that last touched that cell's cell.json on this rev

targets.source: D71 as amended by D82; targets are INPUTS and the scorer never selects one, so the single sweep setting present in every cell is reported as it stands

positive_control.rule: at least two known-good committed arms must reproduce EXACTLY before the table is trusted; a failure means THE READER IS BROKEN, not the arm, and the table is refused and this is reported instead

device_only_floor_note: Verified, not assumed, and verified over ALL cells of the seed INCLUDING the two excluded arms, because the identity is a property of the cells. At seed 6 it is 0.057851 (7 of 121) across all 17 cells, which is the committed value. No seed's cells disagree about their own floor.

comparability.note_on_decoding: Decoding is not a per-cell field. The live2 request bodies fix it in code (`experiments/orchestration/live2/bodies.py`, temperature=0.0, greedy, with the seed read from a committed constant), so two cells share decoding exactly when that file's SAMPLING LINES agree at the code rev their own header records. Those lines are extracted per cell AT its own rev, so the claim is checked and not asserted. Keying on the whole-file blob was tried FIRST and was WRONG: the two blobs present in this grid differ only in the D150 / D164 `kv_transfer_params` host-offload plumbing, not in any sampling parameter, so a blob-level check reports a decoding mismatch where there is none.
comparability.note_on_unverifiable_decoding: The cells whose code rev is NOT in this box's object store cannot have their sampling lines read at all, so their decoding is UNVERIFIABLE rather than matched. Each such cell is named per seed. Their own headers record `git_working_tree.dirty` false, so the rev is a clean commit that simply never reached this box; that is a reason to expect a match, not evidence of one, and it is reported as a declared limitation.
